- When sentiment is strongly negative (e.g., < -0.3) over recent days, model tends to overcorrect upward — reduce forecast peak by 5–10%.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., +5%+ in 3–5 days), model often overshoots next period — cap forecast at +3–5% above prior peak.
- If sentiment is neutral or mildly positive (0.0–0.3), model underestimates upward momentum — add 2–4% to forecast mean.
- Model consistently underestimates true price in early horizon (e.g., 1–3 days ahead) when sentiment is volatile — adjust down by 1–3% for short-term.
- When sentiment turns positive after negative streak, model delays reaction — forecast should rise 1–2 days ahead of sentiment shift.
- Mean reversion bias: if 3–5 consecutive days show downward trend, model often fails to anticipate rebound — add 1–3% upward bias in next 3–5 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, model tends to overestimate volatility — smooth out extremes by reducing standard deviation by 15–20% in forecast range.
